heading: LOGOS-MODULE-CAPABILITY-AUTHORITY
text: LOGOS-MODULE-CAPABILITY-AUTHORITY

heading: Abstract
text: Abstract

heading: Abstract
text: Every Capability Authority provider MUST be a local module provider backed by a local module instance.

heading: Abstract
text: The provider MAY use direct mode or local transport mode.

heading: Abstract
text: An implementation MAY co-locate or statically link Capability Authority code, but Runtime MUST still represent that code as a direct-mode local module instance.

heading: Abstract
text: Remote facades and host or deployment services that are not module providers MUST NOT be bound as Capability Authority providers.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: 3. Authority Scopes

heading: 3. Authority Scopes

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: For the Core scope shapes, required identity fields must be equal, and every constrained list in the narrower scope must be a subset of the broader scope.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes

heading: 3. Authority Scopes

heading: 3. Authority Scopes

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: Every `actions`, `uses`, `scopes`, `providers`, `routes`, `modules`, `instances`, `modes`, `placements`, and `grant_ids` array that is present in a Capability Authority record MUST be non-empty unless its field definition explicitly permits an empty list.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: Every array whose elements are a set of scopes, actions, uses, providers, routes, modules, instances, modes, placements, method roots, event roots, or supporting grant identifiers MUST contain its elements in strictly ascending bytewise lexicographic order of each element's complete Logos deterministic-CBOR encoding.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: Such an array MUST NOT contain duplicate elements.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: A receiver MUST reject an unordered or duplicate set-valued array and MUST NOT silently sort or deduplicate a received, committed, or signed value.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Runtime MUST obtain this decision before satisfying an `all-runtime-visible` request or disclosing a provider's complete call surface through a module-selected call binding.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: For module-selected disclosure, Runtime MUST obtain one `discover` allow decision for the selected provider and each exact primary or interface contract in its validated call surface.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: If any contract view may not be disclosed, Runtime MUST fail the module-selected object request rather than omit that view or return a filtered surface.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Method-level or event-level route access may narrow which operations the consumer may perform, but it MUST NOT produce a filtered construction input, disclose an unrelated contract, or change the selected contract identity.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: An implementation that needs a separately visible subset of a concrete contract MUST expose that subset as its own exact interface contract.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: For route creation or renewal, Runtime MUST include the allocated route identifier in the requested scope.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: It MUST also include the `access` requested for the route.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: An allow decision used to keep a route or provider session usable MUST contain `valid_until`.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Runtime MUST NOT keep the route or session usable after that time without a new allow decision.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Runtime and the provider-side invocation boundary MUST reject calls, publications, subscriptions, and event deliveries outside the allowed scope.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: The scope applies to local `direct` and `local-transport` module execution and MUST NOT contain `remote-transport` in `modes`.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Direct execution MUST omit `placements`.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: `version` MUST NOT be present unless `package` is present.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: If `artifact` is present, `package` MUST also be present because the artifact identifier is package-scoped.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Outside the initial system-service bootstrap authorized under Section 1 or explicit protected recovery under LOGOS-MODULE-RUNTIME Section 9, Runtime MUST obtain an allow decision before asking Module Loader to realize a direct native implementation.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: The decision MUST cover the module execution operation and every required permission scope.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Runtime MAY allocate the module instance identifier used by the module consumer before loading code; allocation does not make the module loaded or ready.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Outside those protected bootstrap and recovery paths, Runtime MUST obtain an allow decision before asking Module Loader to realize a process, sandboxed process, or container.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: The decision MUST cover the module execution operation, selected hosted placement, and required permission scopes.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Runtime and the selected security profile MUST apply those constraints through their enforcement configuration; authority decisions and grants are not added to the Module Loader-owned realization descriptor.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Runtime MUST reject the operation if the selected execution path cannot enforce a required constraint.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Runtime MUST NOT claim containment against code that can access Runtime memory or unrestricted process resources.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A profile that permits operating-system or platform access MUST define permission names and constraints for every facility it exposes. Relevant facilities include: … process creation, signaling, and execution;

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A profile that permits operating-system or platform access MUST define permission names and constraints for every facility it exposes. Relevant facilities include: … CPU, memory, process-count, file-descriptor, storage-growth, and similar resource limits;

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A profile that permits operating-system or platform access MUST define permission names and constraints for every facility it exposes. Relevant facilities include: … placement, isolation, sandbox, and dangerous host or platform operations.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions

heading: 4. Commitment Requirements

heading: 4. Commitment Requirements

heading: 4. Commitment Requirements

heading: 4. Commitment Requirements

heading: 5. Decisions
5. Decisions
text: An allow decision MUST contain `allowed_scopes` and MUST NOT contain `denial`.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: A deny decision MUST contain `denial` and MUST NOT contain `allowed_scopes`, `valid_until`, `grant_ids`, or `commitment`.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: An allow decision MUST list every grant on which it depends.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Its `valid_until`, when present, MUST be later than `issued_at` and MUST NOT be later than the expiry of any expiring supporting grant.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Runtime MUST verify that the decision's consumer and requested scopes match its request.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Every allowed scope MUST be equal to or narrower than at least one requested scope.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: For every requested scope, an allow decision MUST contain at least one equal or narrower allowed scope.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Runtime MUST enforce every allowed scope and MUST verify that the attempted operation satisfies every narrowing introduced by those scopes.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Runtime MUST require a subject to satisfy at least one complete alternative and every narrowing shared by those alternatives.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Runtime MUST NOT combine selector fields from different alternatives to admit a subject that no individual alternative permits.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: An allow decision that omits coverage for a requested scope, broadens a requested scope, or contains an allowed scope that Runtime cannot enforce is malformed and MUST fail closed as an evaluation failure.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: If `valid_until` is absent, Runtime MUST NOT reuse the decision for another operation.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: If `valid_until` is present, Runtime may cache the decision only under the rules in Section 8 and MUST treat it as expired when the current time is greater than or equal to `valid_until`.

text: Authority to invoke `issue_grant` does not itself permit the requested grant; active policy must allow the consumer to issue the requested scopes to that target.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: If it is present, it MUST be in the inclusive range from 1 through 1000.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: An issued grant MUST initially be `active`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: An `active` grant MUST omit `revoked_at` and `revocation_reason`, and its `expires_at` MUST be absent or later than `now`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: If a revoked grant has `expires_at`, `revoked_at` MUST be earlier than `expires_at`.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The corresponding `policy-change` audit record MUST use the same timestamp.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority MUST verify against the committed transition that authorizations for every unlisted target remain valid for every consumer and enforcement context, including scope and commitment requirements.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Caller-supplied target information alone MUST NOT establish this guarantee.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: If completeness cannot be established, Capability Authority MUST omit the field.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The set MAY be empty and MUST use the deterministic-CBOR ordering and uniqueness rules for set-valued arrays.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The event MUST NOT expose targets the subscriber is not authorized to observe; filtering the set does not preserve its completeness guarantee.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MAY retain an existing execution authorization across the transition only when the authenticated event belongs to the same Authority binding, its previous revision matches that authorization's current policy revision, and its complete set excludes the exact execution target.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST then advance the retained authorization to the event's policy revision without extending its lifetime or scope.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Each retained authorization MUST account for every intervening policy transition; missing, inconsistent, or unverifiable transition information MUST end the authorization.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: A listed target's existing execution authorization MUST end.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Expiry, a processed notification of supporting-grant revocation or expiry, enforcement loss, and Authority-binding or notification-path loss MUST still end the authorization under the effect points defined above.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: A change to an unrelated grant does not by itself end an execution authorization; grant issuance MUST NOT widen or revive one.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: If the notification path is lost, Runtime MUST invalidate every cached decision from that Capability Authority.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST NOT perform another protected operation in reliance on an invalidated decision.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MAY retain allocated routes or sessions while obtaining a fresh decision, but they MUST remain unusable for protected operations until reauthorized.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST re-establish and confirm the grant and policy change notification path before a fresh evaluation may seed its decision cache.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST rebuild cache entries from fresh evaluations as protected operations require them and MUST NOT depend on reconstructing a snapshot of policy or grant state.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: If the re-established notification path is lost, Runtime MUST invalidate every newly cached decision again.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority MUST emit `grant_changed` when a grant is issued, revoked, or becomes expired.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST emit `policy_changed` whenever active policy changes in a way that may affect an authority result.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority MUST order each grant or policy state transition with its corresponding event.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The new state MUST become active before the event can be observed, and the event MUST be committed to each applicable active Runtime notification path as part of that ordered transition.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: An evaluation ordered after the transition MUST observe the new state.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Event delivery MUST either succeed according to the subscription rules or cause Runtime to detect notification-path loss and invalidate all cached decisions.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: On `policy_changed`, Runtime MUST invalidate every cached decision from that Capability Authority.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: On grant revocation or expiry, Runtime MUST invalidate every cached decision that lists the changed grant.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority and Runtime MUST deliver a change event only while the subscriber remains authorized for that event and the included grant or policy-change information.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: An event payload, subscription result, or diagnostic MUST NOT reveal a hidden grant.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: After processing a policy-change notification, Runtime MUST re-evaluate dependent operations before admitting another protected operation.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST make a dependent route unusable when the new decision denies the route or narrows its scope below the route's bound scope.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: After grant revocation or expiry, Runtime MUST prevent new dependent operations.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST terminate dependent provider sessions and subscriptions when their continued use would exceed current authority.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: When a required operating-system permission is revoked, its enforcement component MUST withdraw the permission or Runtime MUST stop the execution form.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: An implementation SHOULD cancel in-flight work when safe and supported.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: If cancellation is impossible, it MUST prevent follow-on operations and retain an audit record of the limitation.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Capability Authority MUST NOT directly mutate Runtime lifecycle, provider, route, Runtime Control, or transport-session state.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The container MUST be one tagged `COSE_Sign1` object using CBOR tag 18 from RFC 9052 and the fully specified `Ed25519` COSE algorithm `-19` from RFC 9864.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The protected header map MUST contain exactly `kid`, with COSE label `4` and a `logos.capability_authority.evidence_key_id` value.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The unprotected header map MUST be empty.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The outer object and serialized protected header map MUST use the core deterministic encoding requirements of RFC 8949 Section 4.2.1.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The payload MUST be embedded as a byte string containing the exact deterministic-CBOR claim.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Protected trust input MUST map each accepted `kid` to exactly one producer Runtime identity and one exact 48-byte `SLH-DSA-SHA2-192s` public key.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: It MUST authorize that key specifically for call-evidence signing.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The same key material MUST NOT be used for package signing or TLS authentication.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Two accepted evidence keys MUST NOT use the same `kid`.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The Runtime host or its protected signing integration MUST keep the evidence-signing private key secret and protect it against unauthorized signing.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Evidence under an unknown or revoked `kid` MUST be rejected.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The signed `record` MUST satisfy every `call` audit-record rule in this section.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The `producer` MUST equal the Runtime identity authorized for the selected `kid` and MUST identify the Runtime whose controlled invocation boundary produced the record.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: If `proofs` is present, it MUST contain at least one request or response proof.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Each proof byte string MUST contain exactly one Logos deterministic-CBOR `verified-view` defined by LOGOS-MODULE-HASH-PROFILE.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Every proof MUST correspond to an existing commitment on the same side of the signed record.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: For each proof, the verified-view schema root, hash-profile identifier, hash-suite identifier, and commitment-model revision MUST equal the corresponding fields of the method's defining contract.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST determine that contract from the signed call scope's selected contract and single method declaration root according to Section 9.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Its schema subtree root and value root MUST equal the corresponding signed `audit_value_commitment`.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST then validate the complete verified view according to LOGOS-MODULE-HASH-PROFILE.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST reject a malformed or non-deterministic container or claim, an unknown or duplicate `kid`, an unaccepted header or algorithm, an invalid key or signature length, a failed signature, an incorrect profile identifier, an unauthorized producer, or any record or proof mismatch described above.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Before disclosing a container, the producer MUST apply the same audit authorization and visibility rules as `query_audit`.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Audit queries MUST require explicit authorization and MUST disclose only information the authenticated consumer is allowed to observe.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Audit records MUST NOT contain full route tickets, bearer credentials, private keys, or secrets.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Implementations MAY retain additional local audit detail, but the fields above define the common observation shape.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: An address used to authenticate a consumer, issue a grant to a target, or apply authority MUST resolve to the exact Runtime-known module instance concerned.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Retained grant and audit records MAY name historical module-instance addresses that no longer resolve.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Query filters MAY name those historical addresses; disclosure still requires current authorization for the querying consumer and the records.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: A historical reference MUST NOT authenticate a current instance, establish its liveness, or transfer authority to another address.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: When policy evaluation requires attributes beyond the contract's consumer and scopes, the deployment MUST define a protected attribute-source integration.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: It MUST identify authoritative sources, bind each required fact to the evaluated consumer or target and operation, and specify disclosure, freshness, and failure rules.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: A caller-supplied attribute or claimed identity MUST NOT establish those facts without independent validation.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Obtaining evaluation prerequisites MUST NOT recursively depend on the same evaluation whose prerequisites are being obtained.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Missing, unverifiable, or stale required facts MUST produce an evaluation failure rather than an allow or an invented deny decision.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Attribute snapshots used by evaluation and changes or source loss that can invalidate decisions MUST be ordered with the policy-revision transitions and `policy_changed` event commitment required by Section 8.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: An evaluation after such a transition MUST NOT issue a decision from the preceding attribute snapshot.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Freshness expiry MUST cause the same invalidation no later than the required fact's validity end.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: An allow decision depending on these facts MUST contain `valid_until` no later than the earliest authoritative validity end of any required fact.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: If the integration cannot establish the required change-notification, ordering, and freshness guarantees, a dependent evaluation MUST fail.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Omitting `valid_until` MUST NOT bypass these requirements.

heading: 2. Module-Instance Addresses And Authenticated Call Context
text: Runtime MUST apply Section 8 invalidation and execution-enforcement rules to those transitions, including source or notification-path loss.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: For the Core scope shapes, required identity fields MUST be equal, and every constrained list in the narrower scope MUST be a subset of the broader scope.

heading: 3. Authority Scopes
text: An optional identity absent from the broader scope is unconstrained; if it is present, the narrower scope MUST contain the same identity.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: For this action, the evaluation's `consumer` MUST identify the publishing module instance, and the requested `providers` and `routes` MUST identify the event source and subscriber route.

heading: 3.1 Provider Access
text: Event delivery also requires the subscriber's `subscribe-event` authority and MUST satisfy both route event lists.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: The controller invoking recovery separately requires authority for its Runtime Control request; its authority MUST NOT replace the execution origin's.

heading: 3.3 Module Execution And The Loader Boundary
text: Mandatory withdrawal of authority, failed-attempt cleanup, and cleanup under an accepted Runtime shutdown MUST NOT depend on a fresh ordinary `stop` grant or the target module's consent.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A profile claiming per-module device restrictions MUST identify the consent principal and the controls preventing a denied module from bypassing the enforcement component.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: Process separation, executable signing, or a granted application permission alone MUST NOT establish that claim.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: A permission enforced by a module provider MUST define how the authenticated enforcing provider obtains the applicable authorization for the checked subject, resource, and operation.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: That integration MUST restrict the permissions and subjects the provider may check, define decision validity and invalidation, order revocation against protected effects, and fail closed when required authorization cannot be established.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: An ordinary module contract may supply that integration; the checking provider remains its authenticated consumer and MUST NOT impersonate the checked subject.

heading: 3.5 Operating-System And Profile-Defined Permissions
text: Grant inspection, grant identifiers, and possession of a module-instance address MUST NOT substitute for authorization.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Capability Authority MUST allocate collision-resistant decision identifiers across independent issuers, restarts, replacements, and restoration or cloning of persisted application state.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: A restored counter or pseudorandom-generator state alone MUST NOT establish identifier separation from earlier decisions or other issuers.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: Allocation MUST use independent protected entropy or an issuer namespace and allocation mechanism that preserve that separation.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: An identifier known to identify another decision MUST NOT be reused; if reliable allocation is unavailable, evaluation MUST fail without issuing a decision.

heading: 5. Decisions
text: An allow decision that depends on an expiring grant MUST contain `valid_until` no later than the earliest expiry of its supporting grants.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Runtime MUST set it only while that authorization remains valid under Section 8 and only for the retained consumer, execution target, and requested scopes.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Runtime MUST reject this field on evaluation requests supplied by ordinary callers, including routed calls.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Capability Authority MUST receive the indication through the Runtime-enforced invocation boundary required by Section 2.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: When deployment policy requires protected execution renewal, Capability Authority MUST reserve finite, nonzero admission capacity for execution-renewal requests that ordinary requests cannot consume.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: This protection MUST cover queued and executing work and retained request and response resources owned by Capability Authority.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Renewal requests MAY fail when their reserved capacity is exhausted.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: When deployment policy requires protected execution renewal through this contract, Runtime MUST establish that the selected provider and invocation path support this protection before starting dependent executions.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Runtime MUST set `execution_renewal` for these renewals according to the eligibility rules above.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Module-requested lifecycle operations MUST NOT consume the reserved renewal allowance.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Protection MUST cover every shared allocation, queue, and dispatch boundary on the selected invocation path, including boundaries before the request reaches Capability Authority.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Ordinary request saturation MUST NOT consume reserved renewal capacity or prevent dispatch progress for admitted renewal work.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Reserved admission MUST depend on Runtime-controlled eligibility; the request field alone MUST NOT be treated as proof of that eligibility.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Runtime MUST bound admitted execution demand according to available renewal capacity, including demand from executions sharing a consumer.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Each resource owner on that path MUST retain charges while the charged work or resources remain owned.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Caller timeout, cancellation, connection loss, or binding replacement MUST NOT reclaim capacity still occupied by that work or those resources.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Uncertain charges MUST remain reserved until the charged work and resources are confirmed ended or released, or their owning instance is confirmed terminated.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Runtime MUST reject dependent execution when the required protection cannot be established and invalidate dependent authorization if that protection is lost.

heading: 5.1 Execution Renewal Admission
text: Runtime MUST continue to enforce authorization expiry and invalidation under Section 8.

text: Otherwise, an explicitly authorized replacement requires a new grant identifier and records its own issuer; it MUST NOT rewrite historical grant provenance.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Continuation MUST select only grant IDs strictly greater than the last returned ID, using the current grant state and current observation authority.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Each response returns at most the applicable limit and MAY return fewer records to remain within the Core Transport message-size ceiling.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: A response MUST contain `next_cursor` only when another matching visible record remains.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Capability Authority MAY expire cursors under a documented retention policy.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Capability Authority MUST NOT transfer a grant's target or rewrite its scopes because another instance has the same module name, package, contract, or state assignment.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: A deployment replacing the Authority contract MUST define how retained grants, decisions, and audit records bound to the previous contract remain interpretable.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Historical records MUST retain their original contract attribution and MUST NOT be rewritten as if a decision had been made under different scope semantics.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation
text: Records not representable under the replacement contract MUST remain available through the deployment's documented historical-retention mechanism, subject to their original disclosure rules, for the required retention period.

heading: 6. Grants And Revocation

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST order that processing with admission of dependent protected operations and MUST apply invalidation before subsequent admission.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Time-based expiry remains effective at its defined deadline and MUST NOT wait for notification.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST NOT use an allow decision invalidated by an already processed notification to authorize an operation, populate a cache or establish execution authorization.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST distinguish each establishment, replacement, or re-establishment after required-path loss by a fresh protected binding generation.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Loss or replacement of a binding MUST close admission under its generation, invalidate its cached decisions, and end its dependent execution authorizations under this section before replacement authorization can be used.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST associate evaluations and notifications with their delivering generation and MUST NOT let stale results or callbacks affect a replacement binding.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Equal provider addresses or policy revision values MUST NOT establish binding continuity.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: A new binding MAY begin with any positive policy revision; it MUST NOT revive authority from an earlier binding.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: When an execution authorization ends, Runtime MUST withdraw the dependent execution access and initiate required termination without waiting for re-evaluation or a renewal response.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: A retryable failure during proactive renewal MAY leave the existing authorization in force only while it independently remains valid under this section.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: It MUST NOT extend that authorization, override an explicit denial or invalidation, or create an expiry grace interval.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: A denial of continued execution, expired authorization, or loss of a required validity condition MUST stop dependent execution according to Runtime's enforcement and cleanup rules.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Runtime MUST establish or re-establish and confirm the grant and policy change notification path before initiating an evaluation whose result may seed its decision cache or establish execution authorization.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The evaluation and use of its result MUST remain associated with that confirmed path and Authority-binding generation.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Later confirmation MUST NOT make an earlier evaluation result eligible for those uses.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: Ordinary consumer routes MUST NOT authorize subscriptions to these events, including through an unconstrained event scope.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: The protected binding MUST authorize the complete information required for its notification coverage.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: An event payload, subscription result, or diagnostic MUST NOT disclose information outside that binding's authority.

heading: 8. Change Notification, Caching, And Enforcement
text: After processing a notification of grant revocation or expiry, or reaching an applicable expiry deadline, Runtime MUST prevent new dependent operations.

text: Capability Authority MUST release synchronization needed by reentrant calls before invoking scoped publication.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: Runtime MUST still check destination and event authority at each delivery commitment under LOGOS-MODULE-RUNTIME Section 7.3.1.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: A grant notification MUST disclose the complete semantic grant fields only when the consumer may inspect them under Section 10 at publication admission.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: A hidden grant MUST produce no ordinary notification, placeholder or identifier at publication admission.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: If the consumer cannot inspect the complete set at publication admission, Capability Authority MUST omit the field; it MUST NOT disclose a filtered set as complete.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: Capability Authority MUST bound retained watches, queued observation work and in-flight publications.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: The provider MUST arrange cancellation observation independently of further state changes or publication attempts.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: Ordinary observation MUST NOT block or consume capacity reserved for required engine evaluation, renewal or enforcement-notification progress.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: An implementation unable to continue a watch within its limits MUST end the affected watch through an ordinary completion or invocation failure, retaining already committed Event obligations.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: Direct publication MUST retain the synchronous callback rules; observation scheduling and resource isolation remain implementation-owned.

heading: 8.1 Ordinary Change Observation
text: The ordinary observation stream MUST NOT replace the complete, confirmed notification path required for Runtime decision-cache reuse.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: The records MUST be ordered by descending `timestamp`, with equal timestamps ordered in reverse recording order.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: Equal bounds select no records; if `since` exceeds `until`, Capability Authority MUST return `invalid-request`.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: The record MUST contain the `decision_id` of the allow decision actually applied to authorize the call and the exact enforced call scope.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: At successful call admission, Runtime MUST capture that decision, the enforced scope, and its applicable retention requirements as one consistent snapshot and retain them through the enforcement outcome.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: The enforced scope MUST be covered by that decision's allowed scopes and include every applicable narrowing constraint.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: A still-valid cached call decision MAY be used; a decision authorizing only route establishment or renewal does not authorize a call.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: Subsequent renewal or revocation MUST NOT replace the captured decision or scope in the call record.

heading: 9. Audit Records
text: When an applied allow decision requires request or response retention for a call, the Runtime-controlled invocation boundary MUST produce a `call` audit record after the corresponding enforcement outcome. The record MUST contain the `decision_id` of the allow decision actually applied to authorize the call and the exact enforced call scope. At successful call admission, Runtime MUST capture that decision, the enforced scope, and its applicable retention requirements as one consistent snapshot and retain them through the enforcement outcome. The enforced scope MUST be covered by that decision's allowed scopes and include every applicable narrowing constraint. A still-valid cached call decision MAY be used; a decision authorizing only route establishment or renewal does not authorize a call. Subsequent renewal or revocation MUST NOT replace the captured decision or scope in the call record. This recording rule does not defer required revocation enforcement. Its `scopes` array MUST contain exactly one of these call scopes: … a `provider_access_scope` with the `call` action, one route, one selected provider, the selected contract, and one method declaration root; or

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The container MUST be one tagged `COSE_Sign1` object using CBOR tag 18 from RFC 9052 with the fixed implicit algorithm `SLH-DSA-SHA2-192s` from FIPS 205.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: An explicit `alg` header MUST be rejected, including one that identifies the algorithm fixed by this profile.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Its `external_aad` MUST be the UTF-8 bytes of `logos.call-evidence.cose-sign1-slh-dsa-sha2-192s`, without a terminator.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST derive this value and the fixed algorithm from its protected evidence-verification context before signature verification, not from the received claim or headers.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The context MUST bind the expected profile, algorithm, `COSE_Sign1` structure, call-evidence purpose, accepted `kid`, exact public key, and authorized producer Runtime identity.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The profile identifier inside the signed payload MUST equal the expected profile after verification.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: A verifier MUST NOT retry with another algorithm, context, or profile after verification fails.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The same key material MUST NOT be used for package signing, provenance signing, TLS authentication, or another signature algorithm.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Evidence-signing keys MUST be generated using FIPS 205 key generation and its randomness requirements.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Signatures MUST use pure `SLH-DSA-SHA2-192s` with the zero-length FIPS 205 context.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The FIPS 205 pure-mode prefix is applied by those operations and MUST NOT be added again to their message input.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: HashSLH-DSA, an additional prehash, another parameter set, and a nonempty context MUST NOT be used.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Signers SHOULD use FIPS 205 hedged signing with fresh randomness and MUST fail signing if required randomness cannot be obtained.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Verifiers MUST accept both deterministic and hedged signatures that satisfy the same FIPS 205 verification procedure.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST apply FIPS 205 `slh_verify` and accept only its successful result; it MUST NOT truncate, pad, normalize, or otherwise repair a key or signature.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Empty side arrays MUST be omitted, and `proofs` MUST be omitted when neither side has a proof.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Within each side, proofs MUST be ordered by strictly ascending bytewise lexicographic order of the complete Logos deterministic-CBOR encoding of their decoded semantic path, the verified-view field `7`.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: A side MUST NOT contain two proofs for the same semantic path, even if their proof representations differ.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The same semantic path MAY occur once on each side.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST reject duplicate paths or nonascending order and MUST NOT sort or deduplicate a received claim.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The verifier MUST reject a malformed or non-deterministic container or claim, an unknown or duplicate `kid`, an unaccepted header or protected verification context, an invalid key or signature length, a failed signature, an incorrect profile identifier, an unauthorized producer, or any record or proof mismatch described above.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Evidence export uses a protected deployment-defined integration whose selection, authorization, limits, and delivery policy MUST be documented.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Before disclosing a container, the producer MUST authorize disclosure of its complete record under the audit authorization and visibility rules and separately authorize every included proof.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: If the complete record cannot be disclosed, export MUST be denied.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The producer MAY create a new valid container containing that complete record and only the authorized optional proofs; it MUST NOT redact an already signed claim in place.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Every returned audit record MUST satisfy its CDDL variant and semantic requirements, including required attribution, exact recorded scopes and applicable commitments.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Optional fields MAY be omitted only when those requirements permit omission.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: If authorized disclosure cannot produce such a record, Capability Authority MUST omit the whole record.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: If an admitted evaluation cannot produce its required allow or deny audit record without retaining unauthorized sensitive constraint values, Capability Authority MUST fail the evaluation without issuing an allow or deny decision.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The failure record MUST omit those values and preserve its otherwise required attribution.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: If a grant-issuance request cannot produce its required success or denial audit record without violating these retention restrictions, Capability Authority MUST fail the request with `authority-unavailable` without issuing a grant or grant denial.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: The required `issue-grant` failure record MUST preserve every other required field.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: When the complete requested scopes were successfully decoded and validated and their retention is permitted, an `issue-grant` failure record MUST contain them.

heading: 9.1 Call-Evidence Profile
text: Otherwise, it MUST omit `scopes` in its entirety.

heading: 10. Capability Authority Methods And Events
text: Runtime MUST be authorized to invoke it through the protected system-service binding defined by LOGOS-MODULE-RUNTIME Section 9.
